Notes: Implemented from scratch in the classic constant evaluator (``clang/lib/AST/ExprConstant.cpp``): a new ``EvalInfo::PendingException`` field tracks an in-flight thrown value, ``ExprEvaluatorBase::VisitCXXThrowExpr`` evaluates the operand and records it without diagnosing (so it can still be caught), and ``EvaluateStmt``'s ``CXXTryStmtClass`` case matches it against handlers in order ([except.handle]p3, static-type-only -- exact type, or reference/value catch of an unambiguous public base, plus ``catch(...)``). Destructor-during-unwind correctness comes from a single, minimal change to ``ScopeRAII::~ScopeRAII()``'s existing fallback: it now runs destructors when an exception is propagating instead of always skipping them. Deliberately out of scope, as safe under-approximations (reject a valid program rather than risk accepting an invalid one): bare ``throw;`` (rethrow) and pointer/pointer-to-member exception types (not matched, so such an exception keeps propagating rather than being wrongly caught). The ByteCode interpreter (``-fexperimental-new-constant-interpreter``) is untouched by design -- both interpreters are exercised by the shared test suite and correctly diverge on this feature there. See ``docs/CXX26_GAPS.md`` Tier 7 for the full design notes, including the backtrace-preservation mechanism and the one documented ``-Winvalid-constexpr`` precision loss (a throw whose operand needs a nested constexpr call is invisible to that check's deliberately shallow, single-call-depth analysis; the real evaluator still rejects it correctly). Fix C++26 by making the rank-1, rank-2, rank-k, and rank-2k updates consistent with the BLAS
Notes: Not in this CSV at all until 2026-08-24: found by tracing the live draft's ``__cpp_lib_linalg`` value (``202511L``) back through ``cplusplus/draft`` commit history to identify what it actually requires, rather than leaving the gap between it and this fork's ``202311L`` unverified (see P1673R13's row). Of its four required changes: (1) updating (E-taking) overloads for every rank-1/2/k/2k update, (2) overwriting-not-accumulating semantics for the alpha-only overloads, and (4) alpha-only overloads plus the ``scalar``-excludes-mdspan/execution_policy constraint were already present/correct in this fork before this session (predating the P1673R13 SFINAE-retrofit work). (3) was genuinely missing: ``hermitian_matrix_rank_1_update`` and ``hermitian_matrix_rank_k_update`` used ``alpha`` directly instead of ``real-if-needed(alpha)``, and all four ``hermitian_matrix_rank_{1,2,k,2k}_update`` E-taking overloads used ``E[i, i]`` directly instead of ``real-if-needed(E[i, i])`` on the diagonal -- both meant a complex ``alpha`` or a not-quite-Hermitian ``E`` diagonal could leave a nonzero imaginary part on the result's diagonal, which is required to stay real for a Hermitian matrix. Fixed in ``libcxx/include/linalg``; added ``hermitian_real_if_needed.pass.cpp`` with inputs whose ``alpha``/``E`` diagonal have deliberately nonzero imaginary parts (the pre-existing ``rank_updates.pass.cpp`` inputs were all already real there, so the bug was untested). Item (2) (overwriting-not-accumulating) was subsequently verified by reading, not just checking, every non-E overload's body across symmetric/hermitian rank-1/2/k/2k -- all confirmed correct. Post-fix review also found the same diagnostic-omitted-real-if-needed bug is not specific to the rank-update family's ``E`` parameter: ``[linalg.general]`` paragraph 4 states the identical diagonal rule generally, for any function reading through a triangle-tagged, ``hermitian``-named matrix parameter. That covers ``hermitian_matrix_vector_product`` and all four ``hermitian_matrix_product``/``[linalg.algs.blas3.xxmm]`` overloads (whichever argument is the Hermitian factor), which had the identical unfixed stored-vs-conjugated-vs-diagonal branch. Fixed those 6 call sites too, with 3 more test cases (one per distinct index-pair shape: the vector case and both matrix-product factor orderings) verified against a scratch binary before being added to the lit test. Did not by itself unblock the ``__cpp_lib_linalg`` FTM bump to ``202511L`` at the time this note was written -- that required P3222R0/P2642R6/``std::constant_wrapper``, which landed 2026-09-14 via issue #14's mdspan/submdspan bundle; ``__cpp_lib_linalg`` is now ``202511L``, see P1673R13's row.
